name: Exploring product-truth flows in the Atlas
summary: The user journey through the Atlas /flows view: open the view to see every flow listed, filter by source (mock vs real) and kind (user/data/architecture), select a flow to render its graph, open a step to inspect its acceptance criteria's live status plus the mock records and mockup it uses, and cross-jump from an acceptance criterion back to the flows it appears in. This is how a person sees product truth visually rather than reading JSON. Each flow and step also gets one shareable address (/flows/<flow id>, ?step=<id>); this address layer is specified, not yet built.

steps.label: Jump from an AC to the flows it appears in
steps.human:
The AC detail UI looks up its appearances in the internal map built by flowAppearancesByAc, then offers links naming flow and step/branch. The historical stepId property can identify either node kind. Following a link is UI navigation, not a JSON mutation. [Map producer](leafcutter-web/lib/data/flows.ts).

Today each link is /flows?flow=<percent-encoded flow id>&step=<node id> ([AC drawer](leafcutter-web/components/atlas/detail-drawer.tsx)). The Flows view reads neither parameter, so following one opens the default flow rather than the linked flow and step. The step-link form that replaces it is specified on the next step; old links in this form are redirected by the legacy-link branch.

steps.label: 'Appears in flows' links open the step itself
steps.human:
In the AC detail drawer, each 'Appears in flows' link points at the step link of the node that implements the AC: the flow's canonical URL plus ?step=<step or branch id>, for example /flows/leafcutter/flow-render-pipeline?step=resolve. The '/' inside the flow id stays a literal path separator, never %2F. Branches use the same ?step= form, because the explorer opens the same drawer for a step and a branch. The link is built from the flowId and stepId the appearance map already carries; no new map field is needed. Specified, not built: today's drawer still emits the legacy /flows?flow=...&step=... form described on the 'Jump from an AC' step. Records: FlowAppearance in the [canonical dataset](docs/product-truth/mock-data/leafcutter/atlas-flows.mock.json); screen section 'AC detail: Appears in flows links open the step'.

steps.label: Open a flow from its canonical link
steps.human:
A person opens /flows/<flow id>: a link pasted into chat, a ticket or a PR, a typed address or a bookmark. The flow id is everything after /flows/, with its '/' literal, for example /flows/leafcutter/flow-render-pipeline. The Atlas answers 200 and opens on that flow, selected and drawn, with no drawer open. The Source and Kind filters switch to the flow's own values and Realization is All, so the selector lists the linked flow instead of falling back to the first flow of the default filters. The breadcrumb shows only that flow, because a canonical URL names one flow, not the drill path that led to it. Specified, not built: today the Flows view reads no address and always opens leafcutter/deliver-a-feature ([Flows view](leafcutter-web/components/flows/flows-view.tsx)). Records: FlowRoute route-shared-data-pipeline, route-shared-mock-journey, route-bookmarked-agent-subflow and route-shared-architecture-map.

steps.label: Opening a drawer writes ?step= in place
steps.human:
Clicking a step or branch opens its drawer and rewrites the address to the flow's canonical URL plus ?step=<id> with history replace: the current entry changes in place and no Back entry is added, so the address always shares exactly what is on screen. For example, on /flows/leafcutter/deliver-a-feature, clicking 'Plan' makes the address /flows/leafcutter/deliver-a-feature?step=plan. Owner ruling 1 (2026-10-09): on the bare /flows entry the same click replaces /flows with the default flow's canonical URL plus ?step=<id>, so /flows also becomes /flows/leafcutter/deliver-a-feature?step=plan, and closing that drawer then leaves /flows/leafcutter/deliver-a-feature, never /flows again. The drawer's contents are those of the 'Open a step' step. Records: FlowNavigation nav-drawer-replace-2 and nav-drawer-on-bare-flows-1 to -3.

steps.label: Closing the drawer removes ?step= in place
steps.human:
Closing the drawer with its X button, or by clicking the canvas beside it, removes ?step= and leaves the flow's canonical URL, again with history replace and no new Back entry. After opening, switching and closing drawers, one Back press still leaves the flow, because none of those actions added an entry. A drawer opened on the bare /flows entry closes to /flows/leafcutter/deliver-a-feature, never back to /flows (owner ruling 1). Records: FlowNavigation nav-drawer-replace-4, nav-drawer-in-history-4 and nav-drawer-on-bare-flows-3.

steps.label: Select, drill and breadcrumb push the flow's URL
steps.human:
Picking a flow in the selector, drilling into a sub-flow (on the node, or with 'Open sub-flow' in its drawer) and clicking a breadcrumb each push a new history entry whose address is the target flow's canonical URL with no ?step=. Selecting starts a breadcrumb with only that flow, drilling appends the sub-flow to the trail, and a breadcrumb cuts the trail after the flow clicked. A push drops any forward entries. The trail is not part of the URL, so each entry has to keep it for Back and Forward. A Source, Kind or Realization filter change never pushes: by owner ruling 3 it replaces the current entry (the two branches of the filter step). Records: FlowNavigation sessions drill-and-return, shared-mock-journey and recover-from-unknown.

steps.label: Back and Forward move between flows
steps.human:
The browser's Back and Forward buttons move between the entries that selecting, drilling and breadcrumbs pushed. Each entry returns as it was left: its address, its flow, its breadcrumb trail, the drawer named by its ?step= (whatever was last replaced into it) and its Source, Kind and Realization filters. An entry that a filter change rewrote returns as that change left it (nav-filter-replace-6 and -7), and an unknown ?step= that a real drawer replaced never comes back (nav-clear-step-notice-4). Because drawer actions and filter changes only replace, Back never steps through them. Back onto an unknown-flow entry shows the 'Flow not found' notice again. Restoring each entry's filters is the dataset's assumption; the owner has not ruled on it. Records: FlowNavigation sessions drill-and-return, drawer-in-history, select-from-open-drawer, recover-from-unknown, clear-step-notice and filter-replace.

branches.human:
Owner ruling 3 (2026-10-09): when a Source, Kind or Realization change leaves the entry flow (the first breadcrumb) out of scope, the first flow the selector lists under the new filters renders, as today, with a one-flow breadcrumb and no drawer, and the current history entry is replaced with that flow's canonical URL, with no ?step= and no new Back entry. Back returns to the /flows/leafcutter/deliver-a-feature entry, and Forward returns the define-a-feature entry as the filter change left it. Not modelled by the dataset: a filter change while the 'Flow not found' notice shows. Records: FlowNavigation nav-filter-replace-1 to -3 and -5 to -7.

No flow is drawn and the breadcrumb is empty: the view never falls back to the default or any other flow. The bad address stays in the address bar so it can be corrected. A ?step= on an unknown flow is not looked at: only the 'Flow not found' notice shows. Records: FlowRoute route-unknown-typo, route-unknown-product-only, route-unknown-step-suffix and route-unknown-flow-with-step.

branches.human:
Owner ruling 2 (2026-10-09): while the 'Step not found' notice shows, opening a real step's or branch's drawer clears the notice and replaces the unknown ?step= value with that node's id, with history replace and no new Back entry, so the notice never outlives the unknown value and the unknown value never outlives the notice. Contract fields and examples (generated)
No JSON handoff: A click on a real step or branch node clears the 'Step not found' state, opens that node's drawer and rewrites the current history entry's unknown ?step= value to the node's id in place (history replace). No request is made and no JSON payload is passed.

branches.condition: the link is a legacy /flows?flow=<id>&step=<step> link
branches.label: Legacy ?flow= link redirects (308)
branches.human:
Links in the old form the AC drawer used to emit, /flows?flow=<id with its '/' percent-encoded as %2F>&step=<step>, answer a permanent 308 redirect to the step link /flows/<id>?step=<step> with the '/' literal. For example /flows?flow=leafcutter%2Fflow-render-pipeline&step=resolve lands on /flows/leafcutter/flow-render-pipeline?step=resolve with the resolve drawer open, exactly as a new step link, and the legacy URL does not stay in the tab's history. Not modelled by the dataset: a legacy ?flow= link without &step=. Record: FlowRoute route-legacy-step-link.

The page it lands on is the step link documented on openStepLink.

branches.condition: another step's or branch's drawer is already open
branches.label: Switch from one drawer to another
branches.human:
With one drawer open, clicking another step or branch swaps the single ?step= value instead of adding a second, again with history replace and no new Back entry: from ?step=plan, clicking 'Build' gives /flows/leafcutter/deliver-a-feature?step=build with only the Build drawer open. Open build detail from the mockup: today's drawer lays a full-canvas scrim that closes the drawer on click, so a direct switch needs the click to reach the other step node, and how the build lets it through is not decided. The address ends the same either way, because a scrim close followed by a node open are both replaces. Record: FlowNavigation nav-drawer-replace-3.

branches.human:
Selecting or drilling while a drawer is open closes the drawer: the pushed entry is the target flow's canonical URL with no ?step=, and the entry left behind keeps the ?step= last replaced into it. From /flows/leafcutter/flow-render-pipeline?step=resolve, picking 'Inside python-coder (the coder's internal workflow)' pushes /flows/leafcutter/python-coder-internal; Back then returns to the resolve drawer. Records: FlowNavigation sessions select-from-open-drawer and drawer-in-history.

v5: canonical, shareable Atlas flow URLs, from the owner-approved dataset leafcutter/atlas-flows v2 (commit e7c04e5f8) and the mockup leafcutter/atlas-flows-canonical-url (screen atlas-flows-canonical-url, commit 46255a446). Set entities to Flow, FlowRoute, FlowAppearance and FlowNavigation; the steps reach the dataset leafcutter/atlas-flows through the canonical-URL mockup. The flow-level mock_data_ref was left unset so this product-truth commit does not rewrite the back-references of done UXP-520 ACs, whose missing test coverage is ticketed separately. Added steps acStepLink, openByLink, openStepLink, drawerUrl, drawerClose, navPush and backForward, and branches bareFlows, flowNotFound, stepNotFound, legacyRedirect, drawerSwitch and pushFromOpenDrawer, each wired to the mockup screen with one acceptance scenario and empty implements for the business-analyst. Updated the cross step's narrative with today's legacy link form; kept its scenario and its UXP-524 link. Existing step ids, orders, contracts and AC links are unchanged. Approved by the owner at the flow gate on 2026-10-09 with three rulings that keep the URL matching the screen: (1) opening a drawer on bare /flows replaces the URL with the default flow's canonical URL plus ?step=<id>; (2) opening a real step's drawer after 'Step not found' clears the notice and replaces the unknown ?step=; (3) when a Source, Kind or Realization filter change makes a different flow render, the URL is replaced (no new Back entry) with that flow's canonical URL, and a filter change that keeps the flow leaves the URL unchanged. Same day, still v5, the rulings were wired from dataset v3 (uncommitted at the time; FlowNavigation nav-drawer-on-bare-flows-1..3, nav-clear-step-notice-1..4, nav-filter-replace-1..7): the drawerUrl scenario and the drawerUrl, drawerClose, stepNotFound, navPush and backForward narratives now state the rulings; branches stepNoticeCleared (from openStepLink), filterRepicksFlow and filterKeepsFlow (from filter) were added; the history-entry missing binding now also covers filters, which the dataset assumes travel with each entry (not an owner ruling). Readiness, lowered to draft for the gate, is approved again.
